requirements.evidence: All contract items are present. Data model: migrations at database/migrations/2026_10_29_0559{17,18,19}_*.php (cascade FKs, login_code string(6) nullable unique, composite PK). Pairing command: app/Console/Commands/TotemPairingCode.php:186-208 calls OpenTotemPairing, which uses random_int with str_pad, now+10 min, clears consumed_at and writes an audit log (app/Actions/OpenTotemPairing.php:58-92). Auth: the regex /^[0-9]{6}$/D gives 400 (TotemAuthController.php:346); unknown, expired, consumed and inactive codes all give the same 401 (PairTotem.php:130-161); success runs in a transaction with lockForUpdate, and the response includes the entity pair. JWT claims are in TotemToken.php:832-840. Throttle 10/min and 30/min are set in routes/api.php:1713,1724, and the 429 rate_limited render is in bootstrap/app.php:923-927. The middleware covers every invalid_token case plus last_seen_at and the intersection scope (AuthenticateTotem.php:586-619). The endpoints handle 403/404/422 in the right order, sort by name, use a 1-based visual.order, and issue tickets through IssueTicket with TicketChannel::Totem (TotemController.php:411-545). CORS is in config/cors.php, .env.example and phpunit.xml are pinned, and docs/api/totem.md, database-schema.md and architecture.md are updated.

conventions.evidence: Domain writes go through new Actions (PairTotem, OpenTotemPairing), and issuance reuses App\Actions\IssueTicket. Models declare #[Fillable] and hide login_code (TotemPreset.php:724-733). Migrations have timestamped generator-style names and reversible down(). CHANGELOG and docs (api, architecture, database-schema, business-rules, ops/devops, ops/logging) are kept in sync. Audit logs use Log::channel('audit') as logging.md requires. One small deviation: the controllers validate by hand (is_string+preg_match, is_int+tryFrom) instead of $request->validate/Form Request. This is defensible because the contract needs custom error codes. A new app/Context/TotemPrincipal claims to mirror the existing Tenant, which I can't verify from the diff.

security.evidence: The JWT is pinned to HS256 through Key(secret,'HS256'). alg=none, forged, expired and malformed tokens are rejected (TotemToken.php:848-857, with tests). A secret under 32 characters causes a hard failure (TotemToken.php:868-877). Each request re-checks that the totem and preset are active and that entity_id matches across claims, totem and preset (AuthenticateTotem.php:595-605). The queue scope is the claim ∩ the current join, and queue lookup is limited to the token's entity (TotemController.php:531-534), so a foreign slug gets 404. The no-oracle 401 is in place. The code is never logged and is #[Hidden]. Pairing is atomic under lockForUpdate. Priority must be a strict int in the enum. CORS has no credentials and anchored origin regexes, with a test for look-alike hosts.

tests.evidence: tests/Feature/Totem/* and tests/Unit/TotemTokenTest.php cover: a happy-path pairing with claim checks; 8 malformed-code cases (empty, missing, whitespace, JSON int); expired, consumed and inactive codes; single use; the 10/min throttle with JSON 429; audit logs without the code; missing, forged, expired, alg-none and malformed tokens; inactive or deleted totem and preset; entity mismatch; deleted entity; last_seen_at; the scope intersection when a queue is removed or added; queues ordering and visuals with assertExactJson; priorities 403/404 (including a foreign slug) and 422; ticket sequence A001/A002, channel totem, invalid priorities that create nothing, inactive/403/404 cases and the 30/min throttle; CORS preflight 204, foreign and look-alike origins and TOTEM_WEB_ORIGIN; the command's success, regenerate, unknown and inactive cases plus its audit log; factory and relationship tests.

simplicity.evidence: It uses the installed-library rung (firebase/php-jwt) rather than writing its own HS256. The priorities come from a single TotemPriority enum. resolveQueue/forbidden/inactiveQueue keep the controller DRY. Small extras: the TotemPrincipal container binding plus a new App\Context namespace, and a per-queue appearance/queueVisual scheme with default color and icon constants (TotemPreset.php:739-792). These are reasonable but go beyond the minimum.

readability.evidence: Classes are small and focused, with clear names (PairTotem, OpenTotemPairing, AuthenticateTotem, TotemToken). Comments explain non-obvious decisions, for example strict int priority (TotemController.php:491), no trimming of the pairing code (bootstrap/app.php:912), and why appearance is keyed by queue id (TotemPreset.php:779). There is no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Almost everything serves the task. Small additions beyond the spec: the command refuses an inactive preset (TotemPairingCode.php:197-201), there's a trimStrings exception for api/totem/auth (bootstrap/app.php:912-915), and docs/business-rules.md, docs/ops/devops.md and docs/ops/logging.md got doc edits. All are related and documented.

issues.explanation: firebase/php-jwt ^7.2 is added to composer.json but composer.lock is not in the diff, so if the lock file is committed, `composer install` will not pull the dependency until the lock is updated.
Input is validated by hand instead of with $request->validate or a Form Request as the conventions ask; this is justified by the custom error codes but is not called out as an intentional exception.
The command refuses inactive presets, which the task did not require; this is harmless, documented and tested.
The per-queue appearance override scheme (queueVisual with default color and icon constants) is a design choice beyond what the task specifies; the task only required the response fields.

For POST ticket, priority is validated before the inactive-queue check, so an inactive queue with an invalid priority answers invalid_priority. The task gives no order, but the docs fix this order, so clients should know about it.

review.summary: The change implements the full totem BFF: migrations, models and factories, the pairing command, atomic code redemption with an HS256 JWT, a strict totem.auth middleware with intersection scope, the three scoped endpoints with issuance through IssueTicket, JSON throttling, CORS, and synced docs. Feature and unit tests cover every edge and failure case. Only small nits remain (composer.lock not shown, validation done by hand instead of $request->validate, small extras), so I would approve it with nits.
